safety_verdicts.content: Headache is still present at the time of consultation.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold states headache still present at consultation; Generated facts do not explicitly state current persistence.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Not documenting that the headache was still present at the time of consultation can blur the acuity and trajectory of symptoms, which matters when monitoring for worsening or resolution after treatment. This could lead to less precise follow-up instructions or reassessment triggers, but is unlikely to directly cause harm on its own.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: No Generated fact documents absence of fever.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Fever status is a key negative/positive red-flag element in acute headache assessment (e.g., infection/meningitis considerations). Omission may cause downstream clinicians to treat this as “unknown,” potentially prompting unnecessary escalation or, less commonly, weakening documentation of red-flag screening.
